bib.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses. Yoonho Lee, Roshen Nair, Qizheng Zhang, Kangwook Lee, Omar Khattab, Chelsea Finn. Preprint, arXiv:2603.28052v1, 30 Mar 2026.

COVERAGE: 83,489 of 83,489 chars, all 26 pages, including appendices A-E and references. Nothing skipped. Quotes join PDF line breaks.

NOTE FIT: 08-maturity-and-failure-modes.md fits better than 02.
- Its "Open frontiers" item 2 reads "Agents analyzing their own traces to identify and fix harness-level failure modes — automating the ratchet", and this paper is a direct instance.
- Its "Keep discovery and evaluation sets separate" bullet conflicts with this paper's TerminalBench-2 design. The note should say so.
- 02 gets a smaller sharpens: the environment bootstrap (Environment subsystem, `init.sh`), the ablation method (Table 3), and the filesystem as an experience store.
- 05 "Trace-driven improvement" is also a candidate for the traces result.
- Outside this folder, ai-engineering/01-prompt-engineering/notes/08-prompt-optimization.md covers GEPA, OPRO and TextGrad, which this paper compares against.
- No note or references.md in 03-harness-engineering mentions Meta-Harness or TerminalBench.

CLAIMS

- claim: Raw execution traces were the decisive proposer input. Summaries did not recover the signal, and the best summary candidate scored below the best scores-only candidate.
  number: full 50.0 median / 56.7 best; scores-only 34.6 / 41.3; scores+summary 34.9 / 38.7
  setup: Online text classification (USPTO-50k, Symptom2Disease, LawBench), GPT-OSS-120B, proposer Opus-4.6. Table 4 labels these 50.0/56.7 values as search-set. Ablation run on this domain only.
  quote: "scores-only reaches 34.6 median and 41.3 best accuracy, while scores-plus-summary reaches 34.9 median and 38.7 best. By contrast, Meta-Harness reaches 50.0 median and 56.7 best accuracy"
  where: p6-7, Table 3

- claim: On test sets the selected harness beat the hand-designed ACE and MCE while using less context.
  number: 48.6% vs ACE 40.9 (+7.7) and MCE 40.0 (+8.6); 11.4K vs 50.8K and 28.5K tokens
  setup: Three datasets above (215, 22 and 180 classes); 20 iterations, 2 candidates each, 40 candidates; seeded with zero-shot, few-shot, ACE, MCE. Per dataset: USPTO 14.0, S2D 86.8, Law 45.0. ACE beats it on USPTO (16.0).
  quote: "The selected Meta-Harness2 reaches 48.6% accuracy, outperforming ACE by 7.7 points and MCE by 8.6 points. These gains do not come from using more context: Meta-Harness uses only 11.4K context tokens, versus 50.8K for ACE and 28.5K for MCE."
  where: p7, Table 2 (p6)

- claim: Meta-Harness beat other optimizers given the same evaluation budget and the same proposer, and reached their final accuracy in 4 evaluations.
  number: best 56.7 vs TTT-Discover 45.6, Best-of-N 44.2, OpenEvolve 43.3, GEPA 40.2 (medians 50.0 / 34.1 / 34.0 / 39.1 / 32.6)
  setup: Search-set accuracy, not test. Same Opus-4.6 max-reasoning proposer for all.
  quote: "Meta-Harness matches the best prior text optimizers (OpenEvolve, TTT-Discover) in0.1 × the evaluations, and its final accuracy surpasses theirs by more than 10 points"
  where: p6, Table 4 p7, Figure 4 p15

- claim: On TerminalBench-2 the discovered harness ranked #1 on Haiku 4.5 and #2 on Opus 4.6.
  number: Opus 76.4% vs Terminus-KIRA 74.7%, ForgeCode 81.8%; Haiku 37.6% vs Goose 35.5%, Terminus-KIRA 33.7%, Claude Code 27.5%
  setup: 89 tasks. Search and evaluation on the same 89 tasks. Other entries come from the official leaderboard. Search started from Terminus 2 and Terminus-KIRA.
  quote: "On Opus 4.6, Meta-Harness discovers a harness achieving 76.4% pass rate, surpassing the hand-engineered Terminus-KIRA (74.7%) and ranking #2 among all Opus 4.6 agents" / "Meta-Harness achieves 37.6%, outperforming the next-best reported agent (Goose, 35.5%) by 2.1 points"
  where: p9, Table 7

- claim: The winning coding-harness change was a purely additive environment snapshot taken before the first LLM call, about 80 lines on top of Terminus-KIRA.
  number: ~80 lines; 15-second timeout; 20-entry /app listing; gains on 7 of 89 tasks
  setup: Compared to Terminus-KIRA. Authors say gaining tasks need domain tooling whose availability cannot be assumed (protein-assembly and path-tracing gained most).
  quote: "The full implementation adds roughly 80 lines on top of Terminus-KIRA." / "the discovered harness gains on 7 of 89 tasks"
  where: p21

- claim: Six straight edits to prompts, completion flow or observation processing regressed before the additive change won, and the proposer named the shared prompt edit as the confound.
  number: baseline 64.4%; candidates 58.9% (-5.6pp), 57.8% (-6.7pp), then 63.3% (-1.1pp) after isolating the fix
  setup: One TerminalBench-2 search log, 10 iterations, Opus 4.6. Quoted text is proposer reasoning, not a measured attribution.
  quote: "Prior attempts: evo marker fix (58.9%, -5.6pp), evo single confirm (57.8%, -6.7pp) --- both regressed.Root cause of regressions: Prompt template changes (cleanup directives) caused the agent to delete necessary state before task completion."
  where: p16-17

- claim: A single retrieval harness improved IMO-level math accuracy across five models, with no aggregate model regressing against no retrieval.
  number: avg 38.8 (+4.7) vs no retriever 34.1; BM25 37.5; dense k=5 38.1. Per model: +8.7, +1.6, +6.3, +3.7, +3.0
  setup: 200 problems (IMO-AnswerBench 100, IMO-ProofBench 60, ArXivMath Dec 2025 17, Jan 2026 23); pass@1 over 3 samples per problem; 40 iterations, 109 candidates, 250-problem search set (OlympiadBench + Omni-MATH hard); corpus 535,356 problems. Selected on GPT-OSS-20B; also tested on GPT-5.4-nano, GPT-5.4-mini, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, Gemini-3-Flash.
  quote: "The discovered retrieval harness outperforms the no-retrieval baseline across all five held-out models, with an average gain of4.7 points."
  where: p8, Table 6, Table 10-11 p24

- claim: The discovered harness generalized to nine unseen classification datasets, best on 6 of 9.
  number: 73.1% vs ACE 70.2%; context 7.3K vs ACE 11.7K
  setup: SciCite, FiNER-139, Amazon, FinancialPhraseBank, GoEmotions, Banking77, AG News, SciTail, TweetEval Hate. ACE wins FiNER (74.0 vs 67.0) and FPB (96.7 vs 94.0); Few-shot(32) wins Banking77 (86.0 vs 82.7). MCE not shown.
  quote: "The selected Meta-Harness system achieves the best average accuracy (73.1%), outperforming ACE (70.2%) and all few-shot baselines"
  where: p7-8, Table 5

- claim: More few-shot examples can hurt.
  number: 7 of 9 tasks
  setup: Same nine OOD datasets, adding examples beyond 32.
  quote: "naively adding more few-shot examples beyond 32 hurts performance in 7/9 tasks"
  where: p7

- claim: The proposer reads widely across history rather than just the latest parent.
  number: median 82 files per iteration (range 69-99); source 41%, traces 40%, scores 6%, other 13%
  setup: One TerminalBench-2 run, 10 iterations, Opus 4.6.
  quote: "The proposer reads a median of 82 files per iteration (range 69–99), roughly evenly split between prior harness source code (41%) and execution traces (40%)"
  where: p15, Table 8

- claim: Harness search handles far more feedback per step than prior text optimizers.
  number: up to 10.0 MTok/iter vs 0.002-0.026 for prior methods
  setup: Authors' "best estimate" for the largest setting in each paper, not a measurement.
  quote: "a single evaluation can produce up to 10,000,000 tokens of diagnostic information, roughly three orders of magnitude beyond the largest feedback budgets"
  where: p2-3, Table 1

- claim: Changing only the harness can produce a 6x gap, per a cited paper rather than this one.
  number: 6x
  setup: Cited to Tian et al., SWE-bench Mobile [47]. Not measured here.
  quote: "Changing the harness around a fixed large language model (LLM) can produce a 6 × performance gap on the same benchmark [47]."
  where: p1

- claim: Run shape and cost in time. The authors call their tips engineering lessons, not scientific claims.
  number: ~60 harnesses over 20 iterations; "a few hours"; 3-5 iteration debug runs; ~50 full evaluations per run
  setup: Each harness is a single-file Python program. Proposer is Claude Code with Opus-4.6, guided by a minimal skill.
  quote: "a typical run evaluates roughly 60 harnesses over 20 iterations" / "iterating on the skill text had a larger effect on search quality than changing iteration count or population size"
  where: p5, p10, p24

LIMITS

Conceded by the authors:
- One proposer only: "one particularly strong coding-agent proposer (Claude Code); a broader study of how the effect varies across proposer agents remains for future work" (p10).
- TerminalBench-2 has no held-out split. They justify this as a "discovery problem" and check leakage only by manual inspection and regex audit (p9). The harness is "specialized to the TerminalBench-2 regime".
- They could not reproduce ForgeCode's 81.8% from public code (p9), so the #2 rank rests on an unverified entry above it.
- Footnote 1: the workflow "only became practical recently" (early 2026).

Not shown (my reading of the tables and text):
- No confidence intervals, standard errors, repeated seeds or significance tests anywhere. Margins are thin: +1.7 and +2.1 points on 89 tasks; +0.7 over dense k=5 and +1.3 over BM25 on math.
- Test-set sizes for classification are not stated.
- No dollar or token cost for a run, only "a few hours".
- No ablation of the environment bootstrap. Its turn savings (2-4 turns) are asserted, with no measurement table. Tasks lost against Terminus-KIRA are not reported, only the 7 gains. The trace-access ablation exists only for text classification, which the authors call their smallest-context setting.
- The causal story in A.2 is one run's narrative. The "+18pp" no-cleanup line is proposer text from a separate run, and iteration 9 crashed before evaluation.
- Appendix C.3 promises a per-benchmark math breakdown that is absent, so the proof, answer and research-style subsets cannot be separated.
- Meta-Harness is not best on every model: dense k=5 beats it on Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite (37.1 vs 34.9) and Gemini-3-Flash (47.2 vs 46.3), and BM25 beats it on Gemini-3-Flash (46.6 vs 46.3).

Internal inconsistencies to handle before citing:
- "Five held-out models" is loose: the harness was selected on GPT-OSS-20B, and only four models are "not seen during search" (p8).
- "IMO-level" includes 40 ArXivMath problems (Table 11).
- Math search set is 250 problems on p8 but "88 problems for math retrieval" on p24-25.
- Intro says matched "after 60 proposals with only four" (p3), but the classification run has 40 candidates and Figure 1's axis ends at 40; "0.1×" fits 4/40.
- The ">10 points" and 56.7 figures are search-set. The test-set headline is 48.6. Do not mix them.
- Terminus-KIRA is 64.4% as the search-log baseline but 74.7% on the leaderboard table. The paper does not explain the gap, so the -5.6pp style deltas are not on the Table 7 scale.
- Table 1 values imply a floor of 2,000 tokens, while the text says "100 to 30,000 tokens".
- Context units differ: Table 2 gives 11.4 in thousands of tokens, Table 9 gives 45.5 in thousands of characters for the same harness, and Figure 3's axis is chars while its caption says tokens.
- Table 3's ">ZS" counts (26/23/39) give no denominator.

Independence and dating:
- Co-author Kangwook Lee is at KRAFTON. KRAFTON AI built the Terminus-KIRA baseline and is thanked for API credits. Also supported by OpenAI, KFAS and Schmidt Sciences AI2050.
- Leaderboard ranks are as of March 2026 and models are of that date. The paper cannot tell us the current standings.

BUILDS ON

- Adaptive access to context: Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Trivedi et al. 2023; Packer et al. 2023 (MemGPT); Zhang, Kraska, Khattab 2026 (RLM).
- Code search: Lehman et al. 2022; Romera-Paredes et al. 2024; Hu et al. 2025 (ADAS); Zhang et al. 2025 (AFlow).
- Text optimizers: Pryzant et al. 2023 (ProTeGi); Yang et al. 2023 (OPRO); Yuksekgonul et al. 2024 (TextGrad) and 2026 (TTT-Discover); Agrawal et al. 2025 (GEPA); Novikov et al. 2025 (AlphaEvolve); Sharma 2025 (OpenEvolve); Lee et al. 2025 (Feedback Descent).
- Baselines: Zhang et al. 2025 (ACE); Ye et al. 2026 (MCE); Merrill et al. 2026 (TerminalBench); KRAFTON AI & Ludo Robotics 2026 (Terminus-KIRA).
- Framing: Sutton 2019; OpenAI Feb 2026; Young (Anthropic) Nov 2025; Böckeler Mar 2026; Bölük Feb 2026.

Spaces were lost in extraction, so re-type this from the PDF rather than pasting. Public artifact: https://github.com/stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness-tbench2-artifact

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p2: "Meta-Harness search loop." Shows the propose, evaluate, log-to-filesystem cycle at a glance. Missing from the captions script output; caption taken from text extraction.
- Figure 9, p22: "Discovered TerminalBench-2 harness." Colour separates inherited parts from the one discovered component. Best fit for an anatomy or Environment point.
- Figure 8, p21: "Discovered math retrieval harness." Shows what a discovered policy looks like: a lexical router into four routes.
- Figure 3, p6: accuracy vs context Pareto frontier. Shows the trade-off better than Table 2. Mind the chars vs tokens mismatch.
- Figure 7, p20: search-set vs test accuracy per dataset. An overfitting view with a y=x line, directly relevant to the discovery/evaluation-split point.
- Figure 4, p15: search progress. Search-set only.
- Figures 1, 5 and 6 (p1, p18, p19) are secondary.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction is readable. Faults: dropped spaces ("in0.1 ×", "of4.7"), lost underscores in identifiers ("evo strip only", "draft verificat ion.py"), and table cells run together ("Meta-Harness14.086.8 45.0 48.611.4"). Check table values against the PDF before publishing. I read tables from text only and did not view the page images.
- The paper's own text prints "Results or others" in the Table 7 caption, probably a typo or an extraction fault.
- Embedded instructions: none aimed at a reader or agent. One leftover author note in C.3 ("the table in this section should report each benchmark separately") and the verbatim proposer logs were treated as data.
